story.title: BJP Criticizes Opposition's Mock Parliament and Challenges Gandhi to Debate
story.summary: The BJP has criticized the opposition's mock Parliament initiative, with MP Sambit Patra suggesting that Rahul Gandhi should be made a 'mock PM.' Patra dismissed the opposition's allegations of electoral fraud, citing that similar events occurred during Congress rule. Additionally, Home Minister Amit Shah has challenged Gandhi to debate the allegations of vote theft in Parliament, coinciding with an upcoming opposition rally in Delhi.

explore_lenses.label: Why is the election chief being targeted?
explore_lenses.title: The dispute centers on voter-roll revision
explore_lenses.summary: The mock proceeding was aimed at Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, not at a completed parliamentary removal process. INDIA bloc leaders link their allegations to the Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and to concerns about how related decisions were made.

claims.text: At the October 31 symbolic proceeding, Mallikarjun Kharge presented six allegations against Kumar, including that he conspired to manipulate elections and acted at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah.

An Indian Express investigation reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi made 14 recorded objections over 10 months concerning voter-roll processes, Form 6, IT-system access and other decisions; the report said some decisions were made without their knowledge or approval.

The Election Commission, in a Supreme Court affidavit, said the three SIR orders were unanimously decided by all three commissioners and characterized individual members’ observations and questions as part of deliberation rather than formal Commission decisions.

An Indian Express investigation reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi made 14 recorded objections over 10 months concerning voter-roll processes, Form 6, IT-system access and other decisions; the report said some decisions were made without their knowledge or approval.

The Election Commission, in a Supreme Court affidavit, said the three SIR orders were unanimously decided by all three commissioners and characterized individual members’ observations and questions as part of deliberation rather than formal Commission decisions.
explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: The competing accounts establish that internal objections existed, but the legal significance of those objections and the validity of the SIR process remain contested.

explore_lenses.label: Can a mock impeachment remove the CEC?
explore_lenses.title: No—the event has no removal power
explore_lenses.summary: The opposition event was political and symbolic. The Constitution gives a Chief Election Commissioner the same removal protection as a Supreme Court judge, requiring action by both Houses of Parliament and then the President.

claims.text: Article 324 provides that a Chief Election Commissioner may be removed only in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court judge.

For a Supreme Court judge, Article 124 requires an address from each House of Parliament, supported by a majority of that House’s total membership and at least two-thirds of members present and voting, on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity; the President then issues the removal order.
The October 31 event was described as a symbolic or “public impeachment” held by INDIA bloc leaders, rather than a motion taken up by either chamber of Parliament.

explore_lenses.label: What are the BJP and opposition asking for?
explore_lenses.title: They disagree over forum and evidence
explore_lenses.summary: The BJP says the opposition should pursue its accusations through a parliamentary debate rather than a public demonstration. The INDIA bloc says the allegations warrant Kumar’s removal and frames the protest as a response to alleged threats to voting rights.

claims.text: Amit Shah challenged Rahul Gandhi and Akhilesh Yadav to debate the “vote chori” allegations in Parliament and said the BJP was prepared to convene a special session for that purpose.

Sambit Patra called the mock proceeding political theater, urged the opposition to seek a parliamentary special session if it wanted a discussion, and mocked Gandhi as a prospective “mock Prime Minister.”
At the symbolic proceeding, the INDIA bloc demanded Kumar’s removal and presented its case as one involving alleged voter deletion and electoral manipulation.

Separate petitions challenging the Election Commission’s functioning and alleged unilateral SIR decisions were deferred by the Supreme Court, while the Commission has denied the central allegations in its affidavit.

story_report.summary: The BJP criticized the INDIA bloc’s symbolic mock Parliament proceeding over alleged electoral manipulation, with MP Sambit Patra suggesting Rahul Gandhi be made a “mock PM.” Home Minister Amit Shah challenged Gandhi and Akhilesh Yadav to debate the “vote chori” allegations in Parliament and said the BJP was prepared to call a special session. The opposition’s event demanded the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, but it was not a formal parliamentary removal motion.

sections.heading: Opposition allegations and Election Commission response
sections.body: At the symbolic proceeding, Mallikarjun Kharge presented six allegations against Kumar, including claims that he conspired to manipulate elections and acted at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Shah. An Indian Express investigation reported 14 recorded objections by Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi over 10 months on voter-roll processes, Form 6, IT-system access and other decisions. The Election Commission has said in a Supreme Court affidavit that the three SIR orders were unanimously decided and that individual observations formed part of deliberations rather than formal Commission decisions.

sections.heading: Constitutional removal process for commissioners
sections.body: Article 324 provides that a chief election commissioner can be removed only through the same process and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court judge. Under Article 124, that requires each House of Parliament to adopt an address supported by a majority of its total membership and two-thirds of members present and voting, based on proved misbehaviour or incapacity; the President then issues a removal order. The October 31 proceeding was described as a public or symbolic impeachment rather than action in either parliamentary chamber.

unresolved.text: The legal significance of the reported internal objections and the validity of the SIR process remain contested.
It remains unclear whether the government will convene a special parliamentary session or whether pending court proceedings will substantively test the allegations.

related_stories.title: UK Prime Minister Open to Slavery Apology Amid Caribbean Tour
related_stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has expressed openness to a formal apology for Britain's role in the transatlantic slave trade. This statement comes as King Charles continues his tour of the Caribbean, where discussions about the UK's colonial history are prominent. However, Burnham has ruled out the possibility of financial reparations, despite ongoing demands from Caribbean nations.
